name: GA-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's partisan index favors Democrats by about 25 points
Incumbent Lucy McBath holds a massive cash advantage (~$676K vs ~$100)
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at roughly 97%
Challenger Kevin Martin has raised only ~$10K with no outside support
model.rationale: The district's D+25 lean, McBath's incumbency, and a roughly 60-to-1 fundraising advantage over Kevin Martin all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and prediction markets price her win at about 97 percent. With no competitive polling or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, the race stays at its expected margin near D+27.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a single-digit race, or a wave of outside spending backing Martin, would be the first sign this is closer than it looks.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lucy McBath, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a district whose partisan index favors Democrats by roughly twenty-five points. She was renominated without difficulty and has built a large financial edge, reporting about $676,000 on hand after raising nearly $900,000. Republican Kevin Martin has raised about $10,000 and reports roughly $100 in cash, leaving him little capacity to introduce himself to voters.

Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 97 percent, and no expert ratings flag the race as competitive. No general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on the district's lean, McBath's incumbency, and the fundraising gap, all of which point the same direction. The expected margin is about twenty-seven points, placing the race firmly in the Safe Democratic category.
